questions.q: Which is the best leaving group in an SN2 reaction at an sp³ carbon?
questions.explain: I⁻ is large, polarisable and the weakest base of these, so it leaves most easily. Acetate is a trap: it is the conjugate base of a weak acid and ranks below even F⁻.

questions.q: The correct order of decreasing leaving-group ability is
questions.explain: The weaker the base, the better it leaves: Cl⁻ (from strong HCl) > acetate > hydroxide > amide ion.

questions.q: Which treatment makes the –OH group of an alcohol leave easily in a nucleophilic substitution?
options: Converting it to R–OTs with TsCl in pyridine
Converting it to the sodium alkoxide with Na
questions.explain: A tosylate ester leaves as the very weakly basic sulfonate ion, whose charge is spread over three oxygens; alkoxide formation makes the group even more basic and worse at leaving.

questions.q: In nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr), the usual halide order is reversed. Which aryl halide reacts fastest, and why?
options: Ar–F, because the strong –I effect of F stabilises the anionic intermediate formed in the slow addition step
Ar–I, because the C–I bond is the weakest
Ar–Br, because bromide is the most polarisable leaving group
Ar–Cl, because chloride balances bond strength and basicity
questions.explain: In SNAr the slow step is addition of the nucleophile, not loss of the halide, so fluorine's electron withdrawal speeds the reaction. Applying the SN2 order I > Br > Cl > F here is the trap.
